title: "Is Default UMAP Bad?"
subtitle: "The defaults are not the problem: tuning buys a few hundredths on class and cluster scores. UMAP is: plain PCA beats its triplet accuracy on all nine datasets, at every setting tried"
description: "Default UMAP (n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1) scored against the best of 30 settings picked with hindsight, PCA, default t-SNE and the original space, on nine real and synthetic datasets with three seeds each. Outside one small-class set, tuning n_neighbors and min_dist buys at most a few hundredths on class separation and cluster agreement. Against two-component PCA, default UMAP loses on global layout on every dataset (triplet accuracy on nine of nine, centroid correlation on seven of seven), and no setting closes the triplet gap. It beats PCA on neighbour recall everywhere and on class separation and clustering on most sets. Default t-SNE keeps more fine neighbours than any UMAP setting on eight of nine sets. Small classes (about 10 per class or fewer on subsampled digits) are where lowering n_neighbors helps."

![Is Default UMAP Bad?](./cover.png)

Most UMAP plots come from `umap.UMAP().fit_transform(X)`, with `n_neighbors=15`, `min_dist=0.1` and nothing tuned. The common worry is that those defaults are bad and a search over settings would fix the picture. If so, some setting should beat the default by a clear margin on the same data. This post checks that on nine datasets.

Short answer: the defaults are not the problem. Tuning buys a few hundredths. UMAP itself is the problem for anything beyond local structure. Plain two-component PCA beats default UMAP on global layout on every dataset here, and no setting of UMAP closes the gap on triplet accuracy. UMAP beats PCA on neighbour recall everywhere and on class separation and clustering on most sets.



## Test

Nine datasets, each run with three seeds:

- **PBMC 3k**: 2,638 blood cells in 50 principal components, eight annotated cell types, from the 10x Genomics tutorial cached in [Part 1 of When UMAP Lies](../when-umap-lies/). A wrong grouping here is a wrong cell-type call.
- **MNIST** and **Fashion-MNIST**: 10,000 images drawn from each 70,000-image set (LeCun et al. 1998; Xiao et al. 2017, via OpenML), raw pixels. A new draw per seed. These are the sets UMAP is usually shown on.
- **Digits**: 1,797 8×8 handwritten digits, scikit-learn's loader.
- **Olivetti faces**: 400 photos, 40 people with 10 each, taken at AT&T Laboratories Cambridge (Samaria & Harter 1994). The only set where every class holds fewer points than `n_neighbors`.
- **Wine** (178 wines, three cultivars) and **breast cancer** (569 Wisconsin biopsies, benign or malignant): small tabular sets, standardised.
- **Noisy clusters**: synthetic, five Gaussian clusters in 5 dimensions plus 45 noise dimensions. Stands in for a weak signal in a wide feature table.
- **Nested clusters**: synthetic, three groups of three subgroups in 20 dimensions, labelled by subgroup. Stands in for a hierarchy, such as lineages and their subtypes.

Methods:

- **UMAP default** (McInnes et al. 2018): `n_neighbors=15`, `min_dist=0.1`, umap-learn 0.6.0.
- **UMAP grid**: `n_neighbors` ∈ {5, 10, 15, 30, 50, 100} × `min_dist` ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.99}, 30 settings. The best setting is picked with hindsight on the score being reported. That is a generous estimate of what tuning these two settings buys.
- **PCA**, two components, and **t-SNE** (van der Maaten & Hinton 2008) at openTSNE's defaults (perplexity 30, PCA initialisation).
- **Original space**: the same scores on the data itself, where they apply.

Five scores, for the things a reader takes from a map:

- **Neighbour recall**: the fraction of each point's 10 nearest neighbours in the data that are also its 10 nearest on the map.
- **10-NN class accuracy**: 5-fold cross-validated accuracy of a 10-nearest-neighbour vote on the map. Are classes kept apart?
- **k-means ARI**: adjusted Rand index of k-means with the true class count, run on the map. Do the clusters you would draw match the labels?
- **Triplet accuracy**: for 20,000 random triplets (i, j, k), how often the map agrees with the data on whether j or k is closer to i (Wang et al. 2021). Is the global layout right?
- **Centroid correlation**: Spearman correlation between distances of class centroids in the data and on the map. A second global score, reported for the seven sets with five or more classes; wine and breast cancer give at most three distances to rank.

Labels are used only to score. No method sees them.

## Results

::: {#cell-fig-verdict .cell execution_count=2}

PANELS = [
    ("neighbor recall", "Neighbour recall"),
    ("kNN accuracy", "10-NN class accuracy"),
    ("k-means ARI", "k-means ARI"),

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Grey bar: range of UMAP's 30 settings (mean over three seeds each). Circle: UMAP default. Square: t-SNE default. Diamond: PCA. Tick (class accuracy and k-means ARI only): the same score in the original space.](index_files/figure-html/fig-verdict-output-1.png){#fig-verdict fig-alt='Four panels, one row per dataset. On class accuracy the UMAP default circle sits near the right end of the grey settings bar in most rows; on k-means ARI and neighbour recall it sits right of centre in most rows, and on triplet accuracy toward the left end on several. On triplet accuracy the PCA diamond is right of the whole grey bar on all nine datasets; on neighbour recall the t-SNE square is right of the bar on eight.'}
:::
:::


UMAP against PCA:

- **PCA wins the global layout.** Default UMAP beats PCA on triplet accuracy on none of the nine sets, and on centroid correlation on none of the 7 with enough classes to rank. No setting rescues triplet accuracy: PCA beats UMAP's best setting on triplet accuracy on 9 of nine sets, 0\.947 against 0\.733 on nested clusters and 0\.866 against 0\.791 on Fashion-MNIST. A UMAP plot shows which groups sit near which less faithfully than a PCA plot of the same data.
- **UMAP wins locally, mostly.** Default UMAP beats PCA on neighbour recall on 9 of nine sets, on class accuracy on 7 and on k-means ARI on 6. PCA clusters better on PBMC 3k\, wine\, noisy clusters. On MNIST, UMAP's class accuracy is 0\.941 against PCA's 0\.437.

Default against tuned UMAP:

- **Class separation matches the data on most sets.** Hindsight tuning raises 10-NN accuracy by at most 0\.034 (wine) on eight of nine sets. The default lands within 0.03 of the accuracy in the original space on 7 of nine.
- **Cluster gains are small.** Hindsight tuning raises k-means ARI by at most 0\.059 (wine) outside Olivetti, and by 0\.071 on Olivetti.
- **Tuning moves the global layout more.** `min_dist=0.99` is the best triplet setting on 6 of nine sets and adds up to 0\.061 (Fashion\-MNIST), still short of PCA. On centroid correlation the best setting adds up to 0\.183 (digits) and passes PCA on one set of 7, PBMC: 0\.332 against 0\.321.

Against t-SNE and the data:

- **t-SNE keeps more fine neighbours on most sets.** Default t-SNE beats UMAP's best setting on neighbour recall on 8 of nine sets. Olivetti is the exception: 0\.592 for UMAP's best against 0\.574.
- **Clustering the map can lose structure the data had.** On PBMC, k-means on the 50 components scores 0\.867, on the default map 0\.549, and on UMAP's best setting 0\.587. On MNIST the map helps: 0\.712 against 0\.361 on raw pixels.

## Small classes

Olivetti is the one set where tuning clearly beats the default on class accuracy: 0\.593 at the default, 0\.672 at UMAP's best setting and 0\.748 in the original space. Each person has 10 photos, fewer than the 15 neighbours UMAP links each photo to.

Subsampling digits to a fixed number of images per class tests whether class size explains it. Five seeds per size:

::: {#tbl-class-size .cell tbl-cap='Digits subsampled to m images per class. Change in k-means ARI and in 3-NN class accuracy from lowering n_neighbors from 15 to 5 (mean over five seeds), and on how many seeds it helped. A 3-neighbour vote, since a 10-neighbour vote is capped when a training fold holds about 6 images per class.' execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def paired(col):
    w = CS.pivot_table(index=["per_class", "seed"], columns="n_neighbors", values=col)
    d = (w["5"] - w["15"]).groupby(level=0)
    return d.mean(), (w["5"] > w["15"]).groupby(level=0).sum().astype(int)


ari_d, ari_w = paired("ari")
knn_d, knn_w = paired("knn_accuracy")
t = pd.DataFrame({
    "m per class": ari_d.index,
    "ARI change": ari_d.map(s3).values,
    "ARI, seeds helped": (ari_w.astype(str) + " / 5").values,
    "3-NN change": knn_d.map(s3).values,
    "3-NN, seeds helped": (knn_w.astype(str) + " / 5").values,
})
Markdown(t.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True))
```

- **Clustering: yes, at about 10 per class or fewer.** At 8 and 10 per class, `n_neighbors=5` raises ARI on all five seeds, by \+0\.120 and \+0\.060 on average. From 12 up the winner changes with the seed and the average gap is at most 0\.034.
- **Class accuracy: at 8 per class.** There `n_neighbors=5` raises 3-NN accuracy by \+0\.073 on all five seeds, from 0\.785 to 0\.857, level with the raw pixels at 0\.855. At 10 per class the gain is \+0\.016, and from 12 up at most 0\.017 either way.

Even at 8 per class the default map clusters better than the raw pixels (0\.563 against 0\.497); it only trails `n_neighbors=5`. When the groups you care about hold about 10 points or fewer, lower `n_neighbors` to about 5.

## Constraints

- **Hindsight is an estimate, not a bound.** The best setting is picked on the score it is judged by, from three-seed means. A dev-set search does not see that score. A search that picked a setting per seed would do slightly better, by up to 0\.026 here.
- **The 10-NN vote is capped on Olivetti.** A training fold holds 8 photos per person, so at most 8 of 10 votes can come from the right person, in the original space as on the maps.
- **Class accuracy is optimistic for UMAP and t-SNE.** Both maps are fitted on every point before the cross-validation split, so test points helped shape the map they are scored on. PCA, being linear, gains little from this. The map can therefore edge past the original space.
- **Euclidean distance on raw features.** MNIST and Fashion-MNIST are scored on raw pixels, PBMC on its 50 components. Another metric or preprocessing changes what counts as a neighbour, for UMAP and for the scores.
- **Defaults are moving.** umap-learn 0.6.0 warns that its default pipeline will switch to recursive initialisation and the Adam optimiser. That pipeline, at `n_neighbors=15` and `min_dist=0.1`, moves triplet accuracy by −0\.022 to \+0\.080 and neighbour recall by −0\.052 to \+0\.026, set by set. On digits and nested clusters its triplet accuracy beats the best of the 30-setting grid, still short of PCA on all nine sets. The comparison here uses the current pipeline.
- **Three seeds, nine datasets.** The seed sets the method's randomness, the triplet sample, the cross-validation folds and the k-means start. For MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and the two synthetic sets it also redraws the data.
- **Held-out points are a separate question.** Whether a map places new points correctly, and why no held-out loss exists to choose a setting, is [Part 5](../when-umap-limits/).

Defaults. Aren't. The. Problem. PCA. Keeps. Global. Layout. Better.
